clue.text: One old lady's about to make a suggestion

indicators.note: the old lady stands about, or around, the letter for one

parts.note: gran is a familiar word for a grandmother, an old lady
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is on the point of offering a piece of advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts I inside GRAN. A grain of something, as in 'a grain of truth', is a mere hint of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a tiny trace or hint of something, as in a grain of truth.

clue.text: Game involving uncapped footballer's famous brother

indicators.note: the game takes in, or involves, the other letters

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game

indicators.note: without its cap, or top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Peter Crouch is an England footballer

explanation.surface: A sporting contest features the well-known brother of a footballer who has never played for his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncapped' looks like never picked for the national side; it removes C from CROUCH, the England striker.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the best known of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Man maybe listening in passage

indicators.note: listening means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an example of an isle

explanation.surface: A man eavesdrops in a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

clue.text: All good stuff's nearly run out

parts.note: nothing but good stuff means no tat, tat being cheap rubbish

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a homer is a home run in baseball

explanation.surface: The quality goods have almost all sold out.
explanation.walkthrough: TAT is British slang for tacky junk, so all good stuff is NO TAT. 'run' is a baseball home run, a HOMER, which 'nearly' cuts to HOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out is away from their house, not available to visitors.

clue.text: Girl can (when not showing a bit of leg)

indicators.note: the letter a is no longer on display in the word for a can, so it is removed

parts.note: can is slang for prison, a jail

indicators.note: only a small part, the opening letter, of the word leg is used

explanation.surface: A girl can show off her legs, or keep them covered up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is a noun here: slang for prison. Take A out of JAIL to leave JIL, and add L, the first letter of 'leg'.
explanation.definitionFit: Jill is a girl's name, as in the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill.

clue.text: I'm slightly surprised — no PE mocks

indicators.note: no means without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: jeepers is a mild exclamation of surprise
taken as written: physical education

explanation.surface: Someone expresses mild surprise that there is no gym lesson, and jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: JEEPERS is a mild exclamation of surprise; with PE taken out it leaves JEERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeers are taunts, and the word as a verb means scoffs or ridicules.

clue.text: Give an old rogue a traditional send-off

indicators.note: a rogue element is unruly, so these letters behave wildly and rearrange

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bid farewell to an elderly scoundrel with a customary ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaving do is a party for someone departing a job, a customary farewell.

clue.text: Back out on track, colt disappointing

parts.note: c is the racing abbreviation for colt
RY is short for railway, a track
off means below par, as in an off day

explanation.surface: A young horse running poorly is pulled out of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a down-clue placement: colt sits above track. 'disappointing' means below par, as in an off day.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry off is to withdraw from an arrangement.

clue.text: English 19 at sea covering up over slight

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom
the word for a school at sea covers, or surrounds, the letter for English

parts.note: 19 down is school, and a gam is a school of whales at sea
re means over, in the sense of concerning

explanation.surface: An English school is at sea when it comes to covering up a minor offence.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' points to SCHOOL (19 down); a gam is a school of whales. 'up' reverses GAEM (E inside GAM) to MEAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or small, so it is a synonym of slight.

clue.text: Drugs keep working for long periods

indicators.note: to keep is to hold, so the drugs hold the word for working inside them

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, so ES are drugs
on means working, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: Medication goes on doing its job for a very long time.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immeasurably long age, so the plural means vast stretches of time.

clue.text: 3 retreat again in panic — aim for here!

indicators.note: panic means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged
the answer to 3 down means out, so the letters in are put out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Fleeing troops fall back once more in alarm, offering an obvious place to shoot at.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is NOT AT HOME, meaning out: take IN out of 'retreat again' to leave RETREATAGA, which 'in panic' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A target area is the zone you aim at, so the whole phrase describes the spot to shoot for.

clue.text: Caught nurse breaking law — it could be grave

indicators.note: the law is broken open so other letters go into it

parts.note: an act is a law passed by parliament
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse was arrested for breaking the law, which could prove serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' is not serious here: a grave accent is the mark over the e in 'cafe crème'-style French words.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave is one kind of diacritic mark, alongside acute and circumflex.

clue.text: Expulsion of son during trip

indicators.note: the son comes in the course of the trip, so it sits inside it

parts.note: an outing is a short trip

explanation.surface: A boy is thrown out while on a family excursion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting is driving someone out, which is what an expulsion does.

clue.text: Superior but lacking class? Not round 'ere reportedly

definitions.text: Superior but lacking class? Not round 'ere reportedly

parts.words: Superior but lacking class? Not round 'ere reportedly
parts.note: a person so stylish that they look down on lessons, and so are absent from the classroom; the street slang suits someone who talks of 'round 'ere'

explanation.surface: A snooty, unrefined type is said not to be from this neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking class' hints at missing lessons rather than poor breeding; the second sentence plays on the phrase as youthful slang, the voice of someone who drops their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase describes someone who thinks themselves too fashionable to bother with lessons.

clue.text: Cole apart, possibly the world's most beautiful woman?

indicators.note: possibly means these letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is the singer Cheryl Cole, separated, perhaps the loveliest woman alive?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Cheryl Cole, the British pop singer, after her split.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian queen Cleopatra is legendary for her beauty.

clue.text: Undergoing revival — not so crazy about change, possibly

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: saner means less mad
a cent is a coin, an example of loose change

explanation.surface: Coming back into fashion, not so wild about altering things.
explanation.definitionFit: Renascent means being reborn, which is what a revival brings.

clue.text: Repair switch touching live wire

parts.note: to repair to a place is to go there

indicators.note: to switch is to swap round, so the two letters are turned back to front

parts.note: re means touching on, or concerning

explanation.surface: A broken switch is near a live electrical cable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Repair' means go, as in repairing to the bar, not mend; 'switch' reverses the word for touching.
explanation.definitionFit: A goer is an energetic, lively person, which is what a live wire is figuratively.

clue.text: Wales winger dropped from club side

indicators.note: one letter is left out of the word for the club

parts.note: a wedge is a kind of golf club

indicators.note: a winger plays out wide, so it gives the outermost, opening letter of the word Wales

explanation.surface: A Welsh wing three-quarter has been left out of his club team.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture misleads: the club is a golf club, WEDGE, and Wales's 'winger' is its first letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a side or border of something.

clue.text: Liberal Democrat upset about split? Nonsense

indicators.note: the reversed letters go round the word for split
in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to rive is to split or tear apart

explanation.surface: A Lib Dem is unhappy about a party division, calling it rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivel is silly talk, rubbish.

clue.text: Woe! Here is Palin finally running for president

indicators.note: running for office here; as an instruction the letters run about and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: the last letter of the name Palin is used

explanation.surface: A dismayed commentator laments that Sarah Palin is standing for the presidency.
explanation.walkthrough: Sarah Palin was the US Republican vice-presidential candidate in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight Eisenhower was the 34th US president.

clue.text: See 12Across
Withdraw bonus — Tom's disheartened

parts.note: an extra is a bonus, something additional

indicators.note: with its heart, or middle letter, taken out

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: An employer takes back a bonus, and Tom is dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' is a tomcat, CAT, which loses its middle letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull out or remove.

clue.text: Question setter's cheap? Correct

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as I, so setter's is I'm

indicators.note: to correct something is to put it right, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the compiler is really stingy, and is told that is right.
explanation.definitionFit: To impeach someone's honesty is to challenge or call it into doubt.

clue.text: Female physiotherapist has letter

indicators.note: has means the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A woman physio has a letter for you.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across FemALE PHysiotherapist.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

clue.text: Welcoming suspicion-like this religion

indicators.note: the word for like this takes in, or welcomes, the word for suspicion

parts.note: so means like this, in this manner
a hint is a slight suspicion or trace

explanation.surface: A faith that warmly receives a hint of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the traditional faith of Japan, honouring spirits called kami.

clue.text: Publish a lot of lies — time to quit

indicators.note: the letter for time is made to leave

parts.note: a tissue of lies is a whole series of falsehoods

explanation.surface: Someone told to print a stack of falsehoods decides it is time to resign.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue a book or statement is to put it out formally.

clue.text: Irritating article of Sarkozy's in e-book?

indicators.note: the French article goes inside the electronic book

parts.note: a tome is a book, so a net tome is jokingly an internet book
les is a French definite article, as used by Nicolas Sarkozy, the former French president

explanation.surface: A piece by the French president published online proves annoying.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicolas Sarkozy was French president, so his 'article' is French: LES. 'e-book' is a whimsical NET TOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nettlesome stings like a nettle, causing annoyance.

clue.text: Writer has new wife

indicators.note: new means the letters are made afresh in another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An author has recently married again.
explanation.definitionFit: George Bernard Shaw was an Irish playwright.

clue.text: Go quiet after rating's been reviewed

indicators.note: after means the quiet word follows the rest
reviewed is read as viewed again backwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: an AB, able seaman, is a naval rating
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone falls silent once their performance score has been reassessed.
explanation.walkthrough: A rating is an ordinary sailor; 'been reviewed' turns AB, able-bodied seaman, back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash at something is to have a go.

clue.text: Doctor's warning — hospital to be axed

indicators.note: something axed is cut out, so the letter goes

parts.note: a threat is a warning of harm

explanation.surface: A doctor warns that the local hospital faces closure.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor a patient is to give medical care, to attend to them.
